cards.front: Recall a key point about The Factors of Production
cards.back: Land = all natural resources (farmland, oil, water). Reward: rent. Labour = human effort and skills. Reward: wages.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Factors of Production
cards.back: Capital = man-made resources used in production (machinery, factories). Reward: interest. Enterprise = the entrepreneur who organises and takes risk. Reward: profit.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Factors of Production
cards.back: Scarcity means resources are limited but wants are unlimited — the fundamental economic problem that forces choices.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Factors of Production
cards.back: Opportunity cost is the benefit of the next best alternative foregone when making a choice. E.g. if government spends on defence, the opportunity cost is the healthcare that could have been funded instead.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Factors of Production
cards.back: All four factors must be combined to produce anything: a restaurant needs land (premises), labour (chef), capital (ovens), and enterprise (the owner).

cards.front: What should you know about economics exam tips?
cards.back: When discussing factors of production, use the REAP framework: Resources (what factors are available?), Enterprise (who organises them?), Allocation (how are they distributed?), Productivity (how efficiently are they used?).
Man-made goods used to produce (e.g. Interest)
Skills and knowledge of workers (e.g. Higher wages)

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Capital means money in economics. Correct: In economics, capital means man-made resources used to produce other goods and services (machinery, factories, tools). Financial capital (money) is different — it can buy capital goods but is not itself a factor of production. A bank loan is financial capital; the robot arm it purchases is economic capital.
Evaluate whether enterprise is the most important factor of production.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: The Factors of Production
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of The Factors of Production with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.

Every good and service produced in an economy requires inputs, known as the four factors of production: land, labour, capital and enterprise. Land refers to all natural resources — not just the physical ground, but also raw materials such as oil, coal, water, and fertile soil.
